body: @FroMage, Steph, what do you think re a possible #22444 impact ?

>Also quarkus.csrf-reactive.require-form-url-encoded=false does not help as the body is still parsed and cannot be read any more.

Right, the CSRF filter is not processing the body itself, ` quarkus.csrf-reactive.require-form-url-encoded=false` is only there to support cases where HTML forms are used and some methods in the class are not related to the form processing

Due to the return of `Uni` the method is marked as non-blocking. Which is fine, I really don't understand why the body deserialisation should pose any blocking issue, since it's always read before the endpoint is called, and we don't support async reading of the body with things like `Uni<User>` as a parameter.

This looks like a bug in RESTEasy Reactive, don't you think, @geoand ?

Indeed.

I'll have to take a look

I can confirm this is a bug on the RESTEasy Reactive side.

Now I need to figure out how to fix it :)

Hi @geoand, thanks, as far as testing is concerned, you might want to update the already existing
https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/main/integration-tests/csrf-reactive/src/test/java/io/quarkus/it/csrf/CsrfReactiveTest.java#L282

For some reasons I thought it did not matter if it was an empty JSON or not but you can update it to send something simple. Test web client requests go to https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/main/integration-tests/csrf-reactive/src/main/java/io/quarkus/it/csrf/TestResource.java#L120, it should probably be split to have a dedicated method accepting JSON only and be Blocking. 

If you prefer to have a simpler test, then it is fine too 🙂

issue.title: Make sure that @WithFormRead doesn't break body handling
